cli.smoke.test.smoke: A BIND OF THE MOUNT IS THE KERNEL'S, NEVER THE DAEMON'S TO STOP (xfstests generic/409–411, 589 under the symmetric default) — mount, `mount --bind` it elsewhere, a file written through the mount reads through the bind; (a) the kernel's `umount` of the original: the daemon is not signalled, the bind KEEPS SERVING (`.stats`, the file sha-equal), `umount` of the bind drops the superblock's last reference and the daemon exits within two ticks, exit 0; (b) `squeezefs umount <bind>`: the kernel's plain detach naming daemon and mount, nothing signalled, the mount serves on; (c) `squeezefs umount <mount>` with the bind alive: the orderly stop ends its connection AT ONCE naming the bind (red: 30 s of `residency backstop lapsed` ×N groups), the bind answers ENOTCONN and detaches plainly; fsck --offline --scrub 0 findings after each

cli.smoke.test.smoke: A CLOSE BURST COALESCES ITS DRAINS (decision 0003 §AF) — no-open, no write cache: `log` written past inline (its close drains), then a shell holds it open for append and 200 forked `/bin/echo` children write a line each through it — every child's exit closes its copy, a FLUSH with custody ⇒ ONE drains (the first), the rest defer to the reclaim cadence's next tick (drains ≤ 2 + the windows the burst spanned, drains + deferred ≥ 200; drained each, they re-uploaded a whole block per close: 57,000× amplification measured) → the deferred custody lands (owed 0, parked 0) → kill -9 → fsck --offline clean → remount → every line there

cli.smoke.test.smoke: A DEAD MANAGER HOLDING A STRIPED HOT DIRECTORY (rung 10 recovery item 6) — A (the manager) mkdirs `hot` and flips it over K = 64 stripes (the explicit command: A holds the map and every stripe); B JOINED storms creates into it (every one shipped to A, keyed to its stripe) → kill -9 A mid-storm ⇒ B PARKS at T_self (park expiries 0) → remount A (the D0 ladder's same-host successor, term 2; its mount replays its own region — the map, the stripes, the shipped inserts) → B's reclaim lands in the grace window, the storm resumes into the same stripes → `ls` = `find` and the stat digest equal from A and B, every counted name listed → umount B, A → fsck --offline --scrub 0 findings (C17 clean)

cli.smoke.test.smoke: A FULL DATA STORE ANSWERS ENOSPC — NEVER EIO — AT write(2) AND AT THE SYNC POINT, ONE LINE PER EPISODE (charter §8's terminal law, the sync point's half) — two 192 MiB data volumes of 1 MiB blocks, the write cache ON: 100 KiB files written (never synced) until write(2) refuses — the residents' claim on the store (`statfs` free counts it) covers the free blocks, `df` shows under one block free, every refusal says 'No space left on device' → `sync -f` promotes the residents into packs until the store has no block for the rest: exit 1 with ENOSPC, the daemon's ONE 'data store FULL' warning, no error line, no tripwire, fsync_promote_enospc ≥ 1 → fsync of every file: the kept ones answer ENOSPC (the same episode: still one line) and are removed → `sync -f` exits 0 → ten tenants of one pack removed: their block returns, a fresh file lands, the episode closes with its tally → kill -9 → fsck --offline clean → remount → every surviving file byte-equal to the pattern (red on dev: 'Input/output error' from `sync -f` and from dd's fsync, 'syncfs: a leg failed (InputOutput)' and 'fsync ino N: a leg failed (InputOutput)' per sync point — generic/750: 235 + 79 in 19 s; the write cache admitted every byte and the dismount pass FAILED 1,481 residents)

cli.smoke.test.smoke: A JOINER'S CLEAN UNMOUNT AND REJOIN while the manager stays up — mount A (the manager) → B JOINED writes inline, staged and striped files (sha list) → `umount` B (clean: every lease released, the page Free, every staged file promoted; A reads every file sha-equal) → B mounts again at the same mount point: JOINED as appender 1 again (its projection's rows naming appender 1 are a previous incarnation's — loaded unleased), every file of every cycle sha-equal on B, B writes more; three cycles → umount B, every file sha-equal on A → umount A → `fsck --offline --scrub` 0 findings

cli.smoke.test.smoke: A LIVE MEMBER EVICTED AT T_OWNER UNDER THE DEAD MANAGER'S STRIPED HOT DIRECTORY (the flakes ledger's second shape, 2026-10-22) — A (the manager) holds `hot` striped over K = 64; B JOINED storms creates into it → kill -9 A ⇒ B PARKS at T_self → remount A (term 2) → B's reclaim lands in the grace window → B's member beat is HELD (SQUEEZEFS_TEST_MEMBERSHIP_BEAT_HOLD: no renewal, no reclaim beat, every other thread serving the storm) past T_owner ⇒ B's COMMITTERS park the gate at T_self on the member's own clock (its second park, with the beat still held: no commit past T_self), A evicts the silent B at T_owner (`tick — 1 evicted`) and recovers its region → released: the beat's reclaim meets the closed grace ⇒ UnknownLease ⇒ B POISONED (every volume FAILED, the move epoch closed) → the fail-stop: the storm's parked create and a fresh one answer EIO at once (never held), the storm child ends when told, `umount B` completes with the crash shape (no release, no page write; exit 1), A serves `hot` on (ls = find), no tripwire on A → fsck --offline --scrub 0 findings (red: a create held at the move gate for T_park_max per op, the storm child unkillable, the shard hung in wait4; B committed through the hold and its stop released 61 recovered slots: A's lookup wedged past the 51 s request timeout)

cli.smoke.test.smoke: A MEMBER'S CACHED COPY OF ANOTHER MEMBER'S BLOCKS NEVER OUTLIVES THE BLOCKS' RE-USE (0003 §W.2) — two 192 MiB data volumes of 1 MiB blocks, no write cache (every write beyond inline striped) → mount A (the manager) + B JOINED (the dest lease off: its window reads are whole-block fills that deposit) → A writes `f` (two blocks, fsync'd) → B reads it until its tiers hold its blocks → A fills the set to ENOSPC → A `rm f`: the delete recalls B's token and B purges the blocks' keys before it acks (scoped purges ≥ 1 on B) → A writes `g` (two blocks, fsync'd) into the blocks the rm freed → B reads `g`: sha-equal to A's, never `f`'s bytes

cli.smoke.test.smoke: A MOUNT THAT RACES THE PREVIOUS UNMOUNT WAITS, THEN SERVES (xfstests generic/604) — a `--daemon --supervise` mount, 501 staged 8 KiB files (never fsync'd) → `squeezefs umount` in the BACKGROUND and a second `--daemon --supervise` mount of the same set at once, the first daemon's dismount pass held on SQUEEZEFS_TEST_PROMOTION_HOLD (its mount already off the table, its writer lock held): the second mount meets the exiting holder's lock and WAITS — its log names the holder and why, it is alive and unmounted while the hold stands, never BUSY → released: the umount exits 0 (`clean unmount`, `exited (wait status 0x0)`), the second mount returns 0 within the orderly-exit ceiling as the set's MANAGER with `guard_exiting_holder_waits` ≥ 1, every file whole, exactly one daemon of the set alive, the supervisors silent → clean umount → `fsck --offline --scrub` 0 findings; the same cycle on a `--single-writer` set (the suites' posture) and on the SYMMETRIC default (where the join door must not be taken against an exiting manager) (red: `another writer holds the single-writer guard … (BUSY, refusal)` at once on the single-writer set — the release run's `-g auto` stopped at generic/604 — and `device I/O failed` from a join of the exiting manager on the symmetric one)

cli.smoke.test.smoke: A NO-OPEN CLOSE IS THE WRITE-BACK DRAIN (decision 0003 §AF) — format (no write cache: a partial block parks in RAM) → mount with SQUEEZEFS_FUSE_NO_OPEN=1 (the daemon latches the connection at ready: its own `.stats` open, the ONE OPEN answered ENOSYS) → `g` written and read → 1 MiB + 1000 B into a fresh `f` (a CREATE: no RELEASE will ever come) and appended to `g` (no OPEN at all) by plain redirections → kill -9 the moment the last close returned: nothing parked, nothing owed, no RELEASE, ≥ 2 FLUSH drains, ONE OPEN → fsck --offline clean → remount → both files whole

cli.smoke.test.smoke: A RENAME THROUGH A JOINED MOUNT INTO THE MANAGER'S DIRECTORY RESOLVES ITS SLOT MOVE (F8; generic/732 under the symmetric default) — A (the manager) `mkdir A B; touch A/f; mv A/f B/`; B JOINED reads B/f and moves it into A (every object the manager's: the intent's home is B's OWN rotor slot, never slot 0), A moves it back, B again; the mirror (B's directories and file, A moving it, B back); each member's file between the OTHER's directories both ways; a rename whose two parents are two holders' — every rename ≤ 2 s, never the move gate's deadline; every file whole through BOTH mounts, nlink exact, `df -i` equal on both; minted ≡ retired; umount B, A → fsck --offline --scrub 0 findings

cli.smoke.test.smoke: A STREAMING OVERWRITE NEVER WEDGES THE DAEMON — format (no write cache), one 1 GiB file laid down, then ONE job's QD16 1 MiB sequential O_DIRECT overwrite of it (fio where present, else the smoke's kernel-aio writer) long enough to drain the fresh supply and run on block-grant top-ups: every write answered inside the row's bound, fuse_op_watchdog_overdue 0, lock_ticked_reregisters 0, the gauges clean, an orderly unmount (rung-10-fsync-route: a top-up winner parked on its journal ticket under a same-lane minter's spin)

cli.smoke.test.smoke: A STRIPED DIRECTORY ON ONE DAEMON — mkdir hot → the explicit flip (`user.squeezefs.stripes` = 64 through setxattr; getxattr answers 64, a plain directory ENODATA) → 10,000 creates key their stripes (dir_stripe_routed_mutations ≥ 10,000; D's own tree holds the 66 markers alone) → `ls | wc -l` = 10,000 and `find` = 10,001 (the K-way merge, every name once) → a 1,000-move rename storm across stripes, every target present, every source gone → stat's nlink folds a subdirectory in → rm -rf: the striped rmdir is ONE intent → umount → fsck --offline --scrub 0 findings (C17 clean)

cli.smoke.test.smoke: A SYNCFS THAT MEETS A RE-STAGE OF ONE OF ITS RESIDENTS LANDS THE CURRENT IMAGE — a 256 KiB staged file (never fsync'd); `sync -f` of the mount from another process, its promotion of the file held by SQUEEZEFS_TEST_PROMOTION_HOLD between its census lease and its locks, while the file is written twice (a 4 KiB overwrite in place, a 1000 B append: two fresh ring generations) → released: `sync -f` exits 0, no error line, fsync_promote_refusals 0, promotions_restaged 1, the file promoted once → kill -9 (a foreground mount: the ring dies with the daemon) → fsck --offline clean → remount → the file is the twice-written image byte for byte (red: EIO to `sync -f` and `syncfs: a leg failed (InputOutput)` — 1,407 lines in one LTP fs run from ftest01–08's sibling sync() calls)

cli.smoke.test.smoke: A SYNCFS THAT MEETS A RESIDENT ITS LAYOUT NO LONGER NAMES OWES IT NOTHING — a 256 KiB staged file (never fsync'd); `truncate -s 0` of it from another process commits the empty layout under the writer's lock and parks on SQUEEZEFS_TEST_RING_RELEASE_HOLD before its ring release (the window after the lock dropped); `sync -f` of the mount from a third CPU meets the record resident and unnamed → exits 0, no error line, fsync_promote_refusals 0, fsync_promote_superseded 1, nothing promoted → released: the truncate returns → kill -9 → fsck --offline clean → remount → the file is empty (red: EIO to `sync -f` and `syncfs: a leg failed (InputOutput)` — 9 lines in one LTP fs run from ftest01–08's truncates against sibling sync() calls, after the re-stage fix)

cli.smoke.test.smoke: AN ORDERLY UNMOUNT LANDS EVERY ACKED WRITE (fstests generic/029; charter §6.1 'Staged', decision 0003 §AJ) — WITH the write cache: `t` 5,120 B truncated down to 2,048 and up again, its tail rewritten (the staged arm's size-neutral write past the record's image); `s` a striped file with one overwrite inside it (custody parked under the write-back timer); `v` the dance then fsync — all three read whole on the writing mount → the orderly unmount the moment the last write returned → remount → every byte there; then the fsync'd dance killed -9 → fsck --offline clean → remount → its tail there

cli.smoke.test.smoke: AN ORDERLY UNMOUNT LANDS EVERY ACKED WRITE — WITHOUT the write cache (SQUEEZEFS_WRITE_CACHE_PCT=0: every write past inline parks a partial block in RAM): the same files, the same unmount at once, the same remount — every byte there; the fsync'd dance killed -9 → fsck clean → remount → whole

cli.smoke.test.smoke: CUSTODY NO CLOSE COVERS IS DRAINED ONCE IDLE (decision 0003 §AF) — no-open, no write cache, the owed idle horizon at 0 (the seam), the connection latched at ready (no RELEASE would drain `m` either): a writer creates `m` and writes 1 MiB + 1000 B (a parked partial block) and holds its fd OPEN — no close, so no FLUSH follows the write: the class a mapping written back after its fd closed (`fuse_vma_close` at munmap) and an async write landing after its close share ⇒ the ino is owed → the reclaim cadence drains it (parked 0, owed 0, ONE idle drain, no FLUSH drain) → kill -9 with the fd still open → fsck --offline clean → remount → the bytes are there

cli.smoke.test.smoke: DEFRAG --fold AND --meta ON A LIVE MOUNT — format (64 KiB meta nodes, 1 MiB blocks) → three fsync'd striped files held OPEN with 12 sector-aligned 512 B writes parked as W2 extents (parked_extent_bytes ≥ 12 pages) → `defrag --fold <mp>` folds every one in place (12 page DMAs for 6 KiB of user bytes ≤ the §J 8× bound, parked_extent_bytes 0, every byte exact after the close) → a forest of 8,000 files cut to 800 and rewritten 4× → `defrag --meta --throttle 1` runs under the duty cycle: `job cancel` mid-run → cancelled; a second at throttle 1: `job pause` → paused → `resume` → running → kill -9 mid-job → remount adopts it and it completes by plan regeneration → compactions + merges ≥ 1, nodes walked after ≤ before, `fsck --online` 0 findings

cli.smoke.test.smoke: FALLOCATE — EVERY MODE'S LAW (charter §6.6; decision 0003 §BH) through xfs_io on a two-volume set of 4 MiB blocks: `falloc -k` reserves blocks `df` counts at once with the size standing and no device byte written, `falloc` raises the size over them, a read of the reservation is zeros; a write inside it lands IN PLACE (reserved_landings, `df` unchanged, the bytes exact) and the rest of the block still reads zeros; `fpunch` frees whole blocks (`df` returns them) and zeroes the edges inside written blocks (the neighbours intact); `fzero` zeroes a written block without returning its space (fallocate_blocks_zeroed) and reads zeros; `fcollapse`/`finsert`/`funshare` never reach the daemon — linux's FUSE client answers them EOPNOTSUPP itself (`fuse_file_fallocate`'s mode mask), the file standing whole; a full store refuses a hole's write ENOSPC and admits the reservation's → kill -9 → `fsck --offline --scrub` clean (the reservations are references, never scanned) → remount → every law re-read, the reservation's space still charged → unmount → fsck clean; no error line, no tripwire (red on dev: every xfs_io command 'Operation not supported')

cli.smoke.test.smoke: FILE HANDLES SURVIVE A CACHE DROP AND A REMOUNT (FUSE_EXPORT_SUPPORT) — name_to_handle_at on a file, a hard-linked file, a symlink, a directory and a nested directory; `echo 2 > drop_caches` evicts every inode; open_by_handle_at opens each (fstat ino equal, the bytes read back, the directory fd's /proc path is its CONNECTED path through `..` to the root, faccessat through it); a renamed file and a renamed directory still open (the directory at its new path); an unlinked file with every name gone and a removed directory answer ESTALE; after `umount`/`mount` every surviving handle opens again, the nested directory's path resolves through its new parent, the removed ones stay stale
